pr_title: Only include scopeId on link-local addresses when using native transport
pr_body:
Motivation:

We should only include the scopeId when the address is link-local or the scopeId was explicit something different then 0. Otherwise we might get into trouble if people don't expect it included

Modifications:

Ensure we only construct a InetAddress with scopeId if its a non link-local address or it was explicit set by the underlying OS

Fixes https://github.com/netty/netty/discussions/14184 , https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/14189
pr_comments: This was found as part of https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HBASE-27304

issue_context.title: EpollServerSocketChannel resolve IPV6 address with zone identifier
issue_context.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/netty/netty/discussions/14184
Originally posted by **srinihuawei** July 16, 2024 Dear Folks, We are using netty (4.1.101) in Apache HBase. Recently while exploring HBASE-27304 jira (where IP will be used in server communication instead of hostname) in IPV6 environment the EpollServerSocketChannel/EpollSocketChannel resolve the remote address with zone ID which is not expected for HBase operations and further leading to connection issues between client and server. Like eg: 8:10:153:0:0:0:0:15%0 address getting for EpollServerSocketChannel Is there any way to avoid zone ID while resolving the IPV6 address? Note: it works fine when changed to NioServerSocketChannel.

review_comments: Reading through the man page, it sounds like scope is _only_ supported for link-local addresses. Does that means we should omit the scope, even non-zero scope, if the address is not link local?
I asked myself the same but then decided against it as we should only fill it with non-zero when the underlying OS tells us so..
